profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap node, tagged Windstream Communications, sits at 5400 South Miami Boulevard, Unit 134, in Durham, North Carolina, within the Raleigh-Durham-Research Triangle Park corridor. Windstream Holdings is a US telecom and broadband carrier formed in 2006 through the merger of Alltel wireline division and Valor Communications Group, headquartered in Little Rock, Arkansas, and grown through a long series of acquisitions including CT Communications, D&E Communications, Iowa Telecom, NuVox, PAETEC, EarthLink, and Broadview Networks. Significantly for this record, Windstream acquired Hosted Solutions in 2010, a North Carolina-based managed hosting and colocation company that gave Windstream a distinct data center product line built around facilities in Cary, Raleigh, and Charlotte, North Carolina, and Boston, Massachusetts, meaning North Carolina is genuinely part of Windstream documented data center history in a way that is not true for every state in its network footprint. Even so, no source reviewed this session could confirm this specific Durham address as one of the named former Hosted Solutions sites or as any other specifically documented Windstream data center, so that connection remains a plausible but unconfirmed inference rather than a sourced fact. The OpenStreetMap tag itself carries comparatively stronger provenance than some records in this operator dataset, added in a small, scoped 2020 edit that the contributor described as based on a quick photo survey using aerial imagery, with a full address and a link to Windstream own Wikipedia entry, though that survey is now several years old and current occupancy is unverified. Windstream filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2019, emerged in 2020, and more recently completed a merger into Uniti Group Inc around August 2025, confirmed by windstream.com now redirecting to the consumer Kinetic brand site.

This facility has no published power specification, and the operator's specification page provides no IT capacity metrics. The research record shows that Windstream, now a subsidiary of Uniti Group as of August 2025, acquired datacenters in Raleigh, Charlotte, and Cary, North Carolina through its 2010 purchase of Hosted Solutions, but does not confirm a Durham facility under either operator name. No address could be verified for this row despite searches of industry directories, reverse geocoding, and cross-reference with company acquisition history.

Without published power or capacity figures, this campus cannot be ranked by the metrics that determine whether a facility matters to AI infrastructure. The state context shows five facilities in North Carolina with published specifications totaling 50.3 MW, but this Durham site is not among them and has no comparable data to enter that ranking.

The absence of published specifications is itself a fact. Either this facility does not host significant compute load, or the operator does not publish its capacity. No certifications or grid constraints can be assessed from the data on file.
